flawed_step: The proof's key step: given closed C and x not in C, apply normality to {x} and C. This needs {x} to be closed. Without T1, points need not be closed, so the step cannot be justified.
counterexample: Sierpinski space X={0,1} with open sets ∅, {1}, X, so the closed sets are X, {0}, ∅. Normal: {0} meets itself and X, and X meets every non-empty set, so in any disjoint pair of closed sets one set is ∅. The pair (∅, A) is separated by the open sets ∅ and X. Not regular: take C={0} (closed) and x=1 (not in C). The only open set containing 0 is X, and it contains 1, so no disjoint open U containing 1 and V containing C exist.
assessment_summary: Without T1, normal does not imply regular. The Sierpinski space is trivially normal, since every disjoint pair of closed sets includes ∅, but the point 1 cannot be separated from the closed set {0}.
